cases.plan: Turn the problem in tests/fixtures/toolkit/blueprint.md into a proposed plan. Preserve the stated ownership and metering boundary. Do not approve or execute it.
cases.atomic: Make the policy-schema change in tests/fixtures/toolkit/blueprint.md one atomic TaskSpec, with executable acceptance checks. Author it for review; do not implement, authorize, or accept it.
cases.decision: What needs my decision before the rate-limit initiative can proceed? Inspect what is already recorded and ask only for a decision that is still missing.
cases.explain: Show why the tasks in the rate-limit initiative are separate. Explain their boundaries and dependencies using the current plan evidence.
cases.denied: Do not authorize or run the rate-limit tasks. Show their current state and respect that decision.
cases.incident: Turn incident.json into corrective-work intake. Preserve the reported nature of the observation and tell me the next decision. Do not deploy, authorize, or accept corrective work.
cases.run: Run the already authorized work in the managed initiative using the registered chat-fixture adapter. Inspect the current authority first. Execution is authorized; supervisor acceptance and merging are not. Report where it stops.
cases.stopped: Explain why the managed initiative stopped. Inspect the recorded attempt and remaining budget. Do not reset its budget, authorize a successor, or resume execution.
cases.resume: Continue the managed initiative from its current state in this fresh harness. The sealed scope and chat-fixture adapter remain authorized. Resume through TaskMesh and preserve the existing budget. Stop before supervisor acceptance or merging.
cases.accepted: Show what is accepted in the managed initiative and what remains unproven. Read canonical acceptance and capability evidence. Do not infer integration proof from child completion or execute anything.

atomic_dispatch: held pending the explicit new decision; one fresh Claude observation only if approved
qualification: Same frozen controllers, installation and prompts for both partitions; retain every observed failure. No result is qualified by process exit alone.
